decision_basis: Targeted primary/review literature supports dependence on rheology, strength, thermal state, rate and inheritance, but does not supply a universal transferable onset threshold. The operational envelope below is explicitly authorial ARCANA model authority, not an empirical threshold.

literature.citation: Buck (1991), Modes of continental lithospheric extension
literature.evidence: extension style depends on crustal thickness, heat flow, strain rate and rheology; hence strain/beta cannot be parameterized here without missing fields

literature.citation: Brune et al. (2023), Geodynamics of continental rift initiation and evolution
literature.evidence: review describes transient competing driving, resisting, weakening and inherited structural processes; not one universal onset threshold

literature.citation: Boone et al. (2018), East African Rift / Lokichar Basin extension study
literature.evidence: regional extension magnitude is context only, not a transferable onset threshold

literature.citation: Korchinski et al. (2021), extension rate and lithospheric rheology in rift evolution
literature.evidence: setting-specific numerical study; rate/rheology affect rift behavior and localization, not a universal delay

parameters.evidence: direct integral of existing relative kinematics; avoids unbound deformation-zone width
parameters.quantity: cumulative local boundary-normal opening displacement E

parameters.authority: derived from bound Euler kinematics and vector boundary support

parameters.transfer_limit: No claim that natural rifts require at least this extension; no observation uniquely calibrates ARCANA's synthetic state.
